**<mark>ICSG PRESS RELEASE                                             Date Issued: 24</mark>**<sup>**th**</sup> **<mark>August 2011</mark>** 



# **Copper: Preliminary Data for May 2011** 

The International Copper Study Group (ICSG) released preliminary data for May 2011 world copper supply and demand in its August 2011 Copper Bulletin. The Bulletin is available for sale upon request. 

According to preliminary ICSG data, the refined copper market balance for May 2011 showed a production deficit of 80,000 metric tonnes (t). However, when making seasonal adjustments for world refined production and usage, May showed a small surplus of 13,000 t. The apparent refined copper balance for the first five months of 2011, including revisions to data previously presented, indicates a production deficit of 146,000 t (a seasonally adjusted surplus of 51,000 t). This compares with a production deficit of 162,000 t (a seasonally adjusted surplus of 42,000 t) in the same period of 2010. 

During the first five months of 2011, world apparent usage grew by a modest 1% compared with that in the same period of 2010, as an 8% decline in Chinese apparent usage* mostly  offset growth in other regions.   World usage without China grew by 6.7%, owing primarily to increases in Japan, the EU, the Russian Federation and the United States.  On a regional basis, usage grew by 6% in Africa, 2% in the Americas, 10% in Europe, 24% in Oceania and 5.7% in Asia ex-China (decline of 3% in Asia incl. China). 

World mine production grew by around 1.6% in the first five months of 2011 compared with that in the same period of 2010: Concentrate production grew by 2% and solvent extraction-electrowinning (SX-EW) declined by 0.6%. In part, this modest net increase reflects operational constraints that reduced production in 2010 in some regions. Production at three of the four world’s leading producers (Chile, Peru and the United States), that combined represent one-half of the world’s production, was down by an aggregated 1.1% in the first five months of 2011. However, production in China, currently the second leading producer, was up by 13%.  On a regional basis, mine production increased by 1% in the Americas, 3.7% in Europe and 20% in Oceania, but decreased by around 1.5% in both Africa and Asia.  The average mine capacity utilization rates for the first five months of 2011 was slightly lower from that in the same period of 2010 at 78%. 

During the first five months of 2011, world refined production grew by 1.2% compared with that in the same period of 2010: Primary production remained practically unchanged and secondary production (from scrap) increased by 6.8%. Production increases of 46% in Australia (recovery from 2010 operational constraints), 12% in China and 6% in India were partially offset by declines in Chile (-4%), the United Sates (-9%), Canada (-26%) and Japan (-17%). Refined production capacity utilization in the first five months of 2011 was around 78% as compared w

ith 79% in the same period of 2010. The average LME cash price for July 2011 was US$9,619.24 per tonne, up from the June 2011 average of US$9,045.43 per tonne. The 2011 high and low copper prices through the end of July were US$10,148 and US$8,536.5 per tonne, respectively, and the average was US$9,429.95 per tonne. As of the end of July, copper stocks held at the major metal exchanges (LME, COMEX, SHFE) totalled 658,164 t, an increase of 89,982 t from stocks held at the end of December 2010. Compared to the June levels, stocks were up at the three exchanges.
